peak14:53

1 · what the curve showedA tiling tangent doubles the local stop rate mid-demo (*4.2x spike, 159 viewers, 2.0x channel norm*). 2 · evidence at that second“if you leave it too long” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)She pauses the build to warn about excess adhesive — "if you leave it too long it's hard to get off" — before returning to cuts. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 3:18-3:28 and rejoin on "once i did enough for the second row without cutting i moved on to the third". 5 · rationaleThe warning duplicates advice viewers can infer from the scrape footage later at 5:41, so removing it keeps the row-by-row build moving.
drop4:20

peak5:28

peak5:34

peak7:05

1 · what the curve showedAudience ticks up as she explains the 3mm expansion allowance (*+1.7% of viewers present, 54 regained, held 4 samples, 63.1% audience here*). 2 · evidence at that second“an extra 3mm as well” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewound to catch the exact tolerance: "an extra 3mm as well so it'd be a bit easy to slot on" is the copyable number. 4 · how (the next move)Add an on-screen text callout of the 3mm figure at 1:00 so viewers do not need to scrub back to hear it. 5 · rationaleA held replay on a specific measurement means viewers wanted the number and missed it once — a caption removes the friction and preserves the signal.
peak2:50
1 · what the curve showedAudience rose while she demonstrates the sliding clip mechanism (*+3.6% of viewers present, 87 regained, held 4 samples, 49.2% audience here*). 2 · evidence at that second“you can push them to the side” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers scrubbed back to the mount-clip technique: "you can push them to the side to make sure it meets the end panel" is the trick worth rewinding. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load the sliding-clip demo into the first 30 seconds as the promised payoff, then run the full build. 5 · rationaleA held rewind on a specific technique proves that mechanism is the draw, not the plinth itself — surface it before viewers decide to leave.
drop3:48
1 · what the curve showedThe outro cliff loses viewers at more than seven times the channel's usual rate for this position (*5.3x spike, 4.71% vs 0.63% typical, 452 viewers, 40.5% to 28.1%*). 2 · evidence at that second“I'll be moving on to talking about the air con, painting” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)She announces the end and pivots to next-video admin: "I'll be moving on to talking about the air con, painting" releases viewers before the subscribe ask. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 3:51-4:08 and end on the finished plinth beauty shot at 3:50, moving the subscribe ask to a two-second card. 5 · rationaleEnd rank is 280 of 295 and this video underperforms the channel's outro norm by 7.5x, so the wrap-up is the specific problem, not the runtime.

curve100 samples, stored one per percent runtime10:31 gone by 0:3033.4% at halfway53% still watching methodhazard = (present before − present after) ÷ present before at each moment; baseline = mean hazard of the previous 5 moments, floored; flagged when the excess viewers lost beyond baseline ranks high; a rise is a rewind only when no comparable drop precedes it and the lift survives the next sample

drop0:00
1 · what the curve showedThe opening sheds about a fifth of the audience in six seconds, but at a slightly gentler rate than this channel usually loses here (*7.54% stop rate vs 7.95% channel norm, 1,386 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“save this bit for the next video” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The hook promises the splashback build then immediately detours: "save this bit for the next video" pushes the payoff back before it starts. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 0:15-0:24 and rejoin on the skimmed wall so the first thing after the hook is tile going up. 5 · rationaleOpening already beats the channel median by 1.9pp; removing the deferred-content aside protects that lead without touching the hook itself.
peak3:09
1 · what the curve showedA brief lift around the first cut demonstration (*1.5% regained, 67 viewers, held 1 sample*). 2 · evidence at that second“score it on the top” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind to catch the tile-cutter mechanics: "score it on the top... push it down and it cuts it in half." 4 · how (the next move)Slow this beat by 2-3 seconds and hold a clean overhead of the score-and-snap so the move is legible on first watch. 5 · rationaleA single-sample hold means viewers wanted the detail but did not linger; clearer staging can convert the rewind into first-pass comprehension.
peak6:12
1 · what the curve showedA small rewind on the mitred-corner fix (*1.6% regained, 60 viewers, held 3 samples*). 2 · evidence at that second“kills with the UV light” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers return for the problem-and-solution beat: "use this Bostick fixing flush and glue... it can't sit together within seconds." 4 · how (the next move)Name the product and the UV-cure trick on-screen the moment the glue appears, so the fix reads without a rewind. 5 · rationaleThe three-sample hold shows genuine interest in the specific product, not just the moment; labelling it captures that intent first time through.
drop7:03
1 · what the curve showedA 19-second lull after the tricky cut loses three times the channel's usual rate here (*4.6x spike, 3.3x channel norm, 294 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“time to get ready for the grouting” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The cut lands silently then jumps to setup: "time to get ready for the grouting" resets the task without showing the finished tile going up. 4 · how (the next move)Trim 7:02-7:10 of silent hold and cut straight from the profile mark to the tile pressed onto the wall. 5 · rationaleThis is the only flagged drop that runs well above the channel's own norm, so tightening the dead beat targets a real defect, not a habit.
peak9:03
1 · what the curve showedViewers scrub back to the grout-removal step and stay (*2.2% of audience present regained, 69 viewers, held 9 samples*). 2 · evidence at that second“against the cracks not with them” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The moment gives a copyable technique: "go against the cracks not with them so I don't remove more than I should." 4 · how (the next move)Front-load this rule as an on-screen callout the first time grout appears, and tease it in the intro as one of the steps viewers will learn. 5 · rationaleA nine-sample hold is the strongest replay signal in the video and marks the specific instruction viewers rewind to catch.
drop9:41
1 · what the curve showedThe outro loses viewers slower than this channel typically does at 93% through (*0.55% stop rate vs 0.82% channel norm, 347 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“next job is to plan what color” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The core job is finished and the script pivots to the next project: "the next job is to plan what color that I want to paint the walls" releases viewers. 4 · how (the next move)Hold this outro as-is; it already outperforms the channel's own outros. 5 · rationalevsChannelNorm of 0.7x means the ending is a channel strength, not a leak to fix.

drop0:00
